items.title: Agentic AI, Assembled in the Open - Jorge Palma, Microsoft (ASL)
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Agentic AI, Assembled in the Open - Jorge Palma, Microsoft (ASL)

Agentic AI is moving from experiments to production, and Kubernetes is a natural place to think about how these workloads are run. Let's look at how open source can provide a common platform layer for agentic systems, allowing frameworks, orchestrators, compute substrates, and identity infrastructure to come together behind declarative APIs. The goal is a more consistent way to deploy, schedule, secure, and observe AI agents using the cloud native model teams already know.</article>

items.title: The Storage Bottleneck AI Didn't See Coming... Joe Zhou, Juicedata Inc. & Frank Li, StepFun (ASL)
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

The Storage Bottleneck AI Didn't See Coming: Inside StepFun’s Multimodal Production Stack - Joe Zhou, Juicedata Inc. & Frank Li, StepFun (ASL)

Multimodal AI has outgrown the storage systems built for it. Training and inference now mix small-file storms, high-concurrency random reads, terabyte-scale checkpoints, and 100 GB+ model files across heterogeneous GPU clusters, private data centers, and public clouds. The hard part isn't any one workload. It means serving all of them through a single storage access layer that follows compute wherever it runs, whether on-prem or in any cloud. In this keynote, we'll show how StepFun made that move on Kubernetes, TiKV, and JuiceFS. Hardware-aware CSI mounts handle heterogeneous nodes, TiKV-backed metadata scales to more than 10,000 mounting hosts, point-get optimization speeds up relevant read-only operations by roughly 50%, and tuning both the metadata engine and readahead for Safetensors loads cuts read amplification by roughly 71%. We'll share how these improvements were merged upstream to turn production lessons into community gains.</article>

items.title: Kubernetes with Conviction: How Customization is... Jago Macleod, Google & Shaun Hopper, Meta (ASL)
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Kubernetes with Conviction: How Customization is Shaping the OSS AI Ecosystem's Future - Jago Macleod, Google & Shaun Hopper, Meta (ASL)

Just as the Linux ecosystem thrives by separating a universal, low-level kernel from specialized distributions, Kubernetes is evolving beyond a monolithic, "one-size-fits-all" architecture. Forcing a single platform to act as a universal orchestrator for everything from tiny edge devices to hyper-scale AI clusters creates inefficiency and strain.
To solve this, the industry is implicitly defining a lean Kubernetes Kernel—the core API machinery, reconciliation loops, and resource abstractions—as a standardized foundation. Simultaneously, agentic engineering is drastically reducing the cost of software creation and democratizing the operational expertise needed to build upon this foundation.

Join us to learn how building on the Kubernetes Kernel allows power-users to create vertically integrated, purpose-built custom distros that achieve significant performance gains while still crowd-sourcing defect discovery and reliability.</article>

items.title: Cloud Native Without Limits: What Can AI Agents Do for Us? - Lin Sun, Solo.io (ASL)
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Cloud Native Without Limits: What Can AI Agents Do for Us? - Lin Sun, Solo.io (ASL)

In Amsterdam, we explored what cloud native could do with AI agents, MCP, and a drone controlled through natural language. Now it's time for Drone 2.
What happens when AI agents become a natural part of the cloud native ecosystem? Imagine agents that can debug production issues, analyze token spending, automate routine operations, and even make us laugh, all while interacting with Kubernetes, cloud native tools, and MCP servers through natural language, with humans firmly in control.

This keynote explores what's possible when AI agents become trusted collaborators in cloud native. Through live demonstrations with Drone 2, we'll show how natural language and AI agents can transform the way we build, operate, and experience cloud native systems, pushing the boundaries of what's possible while keeping humans in control.</article>

items.title: Salesforce Runs on Heroku: How We Empower... Brandon Schoen, Heroku & Shiva Nimmagadda, Salesforce
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Salesforce Runs on Heroku: How We Empower Every Builder at Cloud Native Scale - Brandon Schoen, Heroku & Shiva Nimmagadda, Salesforce

Salesforce is Heroku's largest customer with over 20k apps. Internal teams rely on Heroku to ship fast . As AI and "vibe coding" lower the barrier to software creation, it's essential to provide the right guardrails and restricted access while preserving an intuitive developer experience.

To satisfy strict security requirements, Salesforce relies on Heroku Private Spaces. Behind the scenes, this isolated environment was re-engineered on a Cloud Native stack while keeping the same developer experience. Cloud Native Buildpacks bring the language & framework of choice, while image rebasing lets the platform patch base OS vulnerabilities across thousands of apps in seconds without rebuilding code.

In this keynote, see how these pieces come together to provide a clear shared responsibility between the platform and the builder: builders own delivering customer value, while the platform silently handles scale, isolation, and security.</article>

items.title: Cloud Native: Built by Humans, Engineered to Evolve - Jeffrey Sica, CNCF
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Cloud Native: Built by Humans, Engineered to Evolve - Jeffrey Sica, CNCF

Cloud native has never stood still. As workloads, infrastructure and the way we build software change, an open ecosystem of projects and people gives us the ability to evolve with them. Jeffrey Sica will give a look at how the breadth of the cloud native landscape and the strength of its community are helping us adapt to AI, increasingly specialized infrastructure and whatever comes next.</article>

items.title: Kubeflow Graduation: Powering the Next Era of... Ron K., Andrey V., Vara B., Ekin K. & Manabu M.
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Kubeflow Graduation: Powering the Next Era of Cloud Native AI With an Open Community - Ron Kahn, NVIDIA, Andrey Velichkevich, Apple, Vara Bonthu, AWS, Ekin Karabulut, NVIDIA & Manabu McCloskey, AWS

Since 2017, Kubeflow has evolved from a TensorFlow controller into a Cloud Native AI platform comprising eleven full-fledged projects, used by thousands of organizations across the AI lifecycle. Today, we are excited to celebrate Kubeflow’s Graduation from the CNCF – and the open community that made this journey possible.
This keynote explores real-world stories from our users, showing how an open, vendor-neutral community is pushing the boundaries of Data & AI infrastructure across the whole AI lifecycle. It will highlight large-scale distributed training with Kubeflow Trainer and MPI, and look ahead to the agentic era with innovations such as the Semantic Operator. By bringing governed semantic APIs to Kubernetes, the Semantic Operator enables AI agents, applications, and BI tools to work with trusted business definitions without relying on LLM-generated SQL. Together, these efforts illustrate how the Kubeflow community is building the foundations for the next decade of Cloud Native AI.</article>

items.title: Scaling Multi-Modal Models and Computer-Use Agents on Kubernetes - Kai-Hsun Chen & Hao Jiang, Hark
items.author: CNCF [Cloud Native Computing Foundation]
items.content:
<article>Connect with the cloud native community and explore CNCF events: https://kubecon.io

Scaling Multi-Modal Models and Computer-Use Agents on Kubernetes - Kai-Hsun Chen & Hao Jiang, Hark

Hark builds multi-modal models and computer-use agents — models that operate software the way a person does. Scaling them means running every kind of workload on the same infrastructure: multi-modal data processing, training, reinforcement learning, and inference serving.

All of it runs on Ray, deployed and autoscaled by KubeRay. But Ray is not only our runtime — it is also our resource management layer, with MultiKueue governing GPU capacity across every cluster we operate. This keynote covers how that fits together.</article>
